rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biology is the scientific study of living organisms, from molecules (DNA, proteins) to the entire biosphere. It encompasses branches such as Botany, Zoology, Microbiology, Genetics, Ecology, Physiology, Anatomy, Taxonomy, and Biotechnology. Living things share seven characteristics: cellular organisation, metabolism, homeostasis, growth, reproduction, response to stimuli, and evolution.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Biology = Bios (life) + Logos (study) = the study of living organisms
Scope: molecule → cell → tissue → organ → organism → population → community → ecosystem → biosphere
Scientific method: Observation → Question → Hypothesis → Experiment → Data → Conclusion

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Biology is NOT the same as medicine or agriculture; it is the foundational science, and medicine/agriculture are applied fields.  ·  Botany studies plants (including algae and fungi in some systems); Zoology studies animals.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the definition of biology, the 9-level scope, and the 7 characteristics of life.  ·  The scientific method is a favourite exam question (6 steps).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Botany: Oryza sativa (rice) — a monocot, angiosperm, Poaceae.  ·  Zoology: Rana tigrina (tiger frog) — an amphibian, Chordata, Anura.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Microbiology includes bacteria, viruses, fungi, protists; it overlaps with botany and zoology.  ·  Physiology = function; Anatomy = structure; they are complementary, not the same.

rows.text: There are approximately 8.7 million species on Earth (only ~15% described).  ·  Biology is the fastest-growing science; over 200,000 biology research papers are published annually.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Biology: the study of living organisms (Greek: bios = life, logos = study).  ·  Scope: from molecules (DNA, proteins) to cells, tissues, organs, organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, and the biosphere.  ·  Branches: Botany (plants), Zoology (animals), Microbiology (microorganisms), Genetics (heredity), Ecology (organism-environment), Physiology (function), Anatomy (structure), Taxonomy (classification), Biotechnology (application).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ~8.7 million species; only ~15% described.  ·  A "characteristic of life" must be present in ALL living things (e.g., metabolism, reproduction); not all organisms reproduce sexually (some reproduce asexually).  ·  The scientific method is iterative; a single experiment rarely proves a hypothesis.
